rankings.rank_justification: Visceral opening of public shaming escalates cleanly into Juliana's electrifying verbal counter-strike against Catherine. Cuts on Juliana's scathing confrontation on tight close-up, maximizing unresolved tension and protagonist empathy.

Launches mid-confrontation at the altar and builds relentless pressure as the usurpers prepare to wed over a chained rival. Concludes on a spectacular peak-rupture cliffhanger as a fireball blasts open the cathedral doors, leaving viewers desperate to know who arrived.

Powerful visual hook and tense escalation through the church aisle as Juliana defies her captors. Catherine's subsequent retort slightly defuses the raw bite of Juliana's previous punchline, though the low-angle posture remains imposing.

Strong visual shock of the chained prisoner marching before jeering high-society peers grips immediately. Catherine's declaration at the altar sets up an intriguing curiosity gap, though it cuts just before Juliana's rebuttal.

Opens with an arresting visual of a chained woman in prison rags entering a cathedral, but the walk down the aisle slows middle momentum slightly. Cuts on Catherine's mocking proclamation, posing a decent status conflict but lacking an explosive peak cliffhanger.

Starts directly with Catherine's verbal humiliation of Juliana, giving immediate narrative clarity though lacking the pure silent visual impact of the cathedral doors swinging open. Escalates Juliana's defiance well, but cuts on Rupert's one-word smirk which provides mild narrative closure.

Captures the visual intrigue of the prisoner walk, but the extended 59.5s runtime plateaus into villain exposition regarding title usurpation. Cutting on Catherine gazing up into Rupert's eyes feels more like an insular subplot scene end than an urgent cliffhanger.
